events.title: IBM RAMAC 305 announced
events.summary: IBM announced the RAMAC 305 on September 14, 1956 — the first commercial computer with a hard disk drive, storing 5 million characters on 50 platters.
events.about: The RAMAC's 350 disk storage unit replaced punched cards and magnetic tape for online random access to data. Random-access disk storage became the foundation of every database, file system, and server farm — from mainframes to cloud SSDs.

narrative.whyChosen: RAMAC introduced the hard disk drive as a commercial product.
narrative.whyImportant: Random-access magnetic storage changed how computers kept and retrieved data online.
narrative.problemSolved: Batch systems needed faster access to records than sequential tape could provide.
